title: Throughput-oriented 8 simple in-order cores instead of few aggressive out-of-order cores
where_in_paper: Introduction / Throughput Computing philosophy / Processor core selection
decision: Use 8 simple single-issue 6-stage in-order SPARC cores rather than 2-4 aggressive out-of-order superscalar cores
alternatives_or_rejected: High-frequency deeply pipelined out-of-order cores with extensive speculation, branch prediction and large caches optimized for single-thread ILP
rationale: Commercial server workloads (web, application, database) have low ILP and high TLP with many cache misses; die area and power better spent on thread count than on single-thread performance, improving throughput per watt
outcome: Enabled 32 threads in same die area as conventional large cores, delivered higher throughput on target workloads at ~72W power envelope
weakest_point: Whether paper explicitly quantifies alternative as 2-4 OOO cores or just says general aggressive OOO approach

title: Four-way fine-grained multithreading per core to hide stalls
decision: Implement 4 threads per core with fine-grained interleaving, switching each cycle to a ready thread, for total 32 threads
alternatives_or_rejected: Single-threaded core or 2 threads, or simultaneous multithreading that issues multiple threads per cycle
rationale: With single-issue in-order core, long-latency loads and pipeline stalls would otherwise idle core; 4 threads hides memory latency, pipeline hazards and branch stalls with minimal hardware
outcome: Keeps simple pipeline utilized without complex OOO or large caches, hides memory latency exposed by small L1s
weakest_point: Exact cycle policy (round-robin vs ready-only) and whether 2-thread alternative is explicitly discussed as rejected

title: Single shared pipelined floating-point unit for all 8 cores
decision: Provide one pipelined FPU shared among 8 cores via the crossbar, not private per-core FPU
rationale: Target commercial workloads have very low floating-point usage; sharing saves significant area and power with negligible throughput impact
outcome: Saved area for more threads/cache while maintaining SPARC compatibility, FP operations routed through crossbar to shared unit
weakest_point: Whether paper says FPU is fully pipelined vs partially pipelined and exact sharing mechanism

title: Small write-through private L1s with large shared banked L2 instead of large private L2s
decision: Per core 16KB 4-way I-cache and 8KB 4-way write-through D-cache, no private L2, and 3MB 12-way shared L2 divided in 4 banks
alternatives_or_rejected: Large write-back private L2 per core and larger private L1s
rationale: Small L1s save area and power and reduce hit time for simple cores; write-through simplifies coherence with 4 threads; shared L2 reduces replication, better utilizes capacity across threads and supports high bandwidth from many threads
outcome: Lower per-core cache area allowed 8 cores on die, shared L2 provides ~12GB/s bandwidth and reduces off-chip accesses for throughput workloads
weakest_point: Exact L1 sizes and associativity and L2 size 3MB vs 3MB 12-way 4-banked may be slightly misremembered, and write-through vs write-through with no allocate policy

title: On-chip crossbar, four integrated DRAM controllers and JBus interface
decision: Integrate 8-port crossbar connecting 8 cores and FPU to 4 L2 banks, 4 independent on-chip memory controllers, and JBus for I/O
rationale: 32 threads demand high memory bandwidth and low latency; on-chip controllers remove pin-limited off-chip controller bottleneck and crossbar provides scalable high bandwidth interconnect
outcome: Provided aggregated memory bandwidth sufficient for 32 threads and simplified multiprocessor system design, contributing to throughput performance
weakest_point: Number of memory controllers 4 is confident but whether paper frames off-chip controller as explicit rejected alternative vs just presenting integrated as choice
